lines.en: I tap on Tsukasa’s name in my phone because it’s what you want me to do.
But that’s okay.
Because I want you to want me to do it.
And I want her to want me to want you to want me to do it.
So it’s okay.
What I’m doing is okay.
: Hello?
Except it’s not okay at all.
: Hey.
None of this is.
: Ah! It’s Jeeves again.
: You’ll have to excuse me as I didn’t save your number the last time you called.
: Should I take that as a subtle hint that you don’t want to see me anymore?
: I never wanted to see you to begin with. You’re not even fit to breathe the same air as me.
: Oh, okay. Well, I guess I’ll just hang up then.
: Okay! Bye, Jeeves!

: Jeeves, I understand that advanced technological devices like cell phones might be intimidating to you, but if you can figure out how to press the “call” button, surely you can also figure out how to-
: I know how to hang up the phone, Tsukasa.
: Then why are you still taking up my time? You should know by now that I am a very busy girl.
: Well, I apologize for interrupting your very busy schedule, but are you able to find any time to fit in some lessons today?
: What kind of lessons?
: Lessons in Love.
Thank you for playing!
: What was that, Jeeves? The reception in your impoverished neighborhood prevented me from hearing you for a moment.
: Just...lessons in general. I don’t have anything else going on and figured now is as good a time as any to get some tutoring in.
: Correct me if I’m wrong, but I’m pretty sure that schedule should be up to me.
: You’re wrong. I’m the educational professional here, aren’t I?
: Former professional, Jeeves. All you are now is an unemployed hack mooching off the 1%%.
: Technically speaking, I haven’t formally quit yet.
: So you’re still on the company’s payroll despite not doing any work?
: Right.
: Now you’re talking my language. But I’m surprised. I didn’t think you’d be calling again after the way our last session ended.
: Yeah, let’s not talk about that. Are you home right now?
: Technically speaking, yes. But it’s not the one you’re familiar with. I’m in my commoner room right now.
: Don’t you mean “common room?”
: No.
: Oh. You mean the apartment.
: Shh! If my shareholders hear that I’m spending time in an apartment, ChinamiCorp is going to steal away even more of the market share than it already has!
: So...am I coming over? Or are you so busy acting poor that you’d rather be alone?
: I suppose I can make some time for the sake of my education. But I will ask you to leave all recording devices at home as I simply can not afford ever being spotted in a place like this.
: Can I bring my phone?
: Yes, but do not be surprised if I ask you to lock it in a safe upon arrival.
: Sure, fine.
: Go ahead and teleport me now.
: Teleport you?
: Like you did last time.
: Jeeves, do you suffer from brain damage? I may be rich, but I can not teleport people. Such a method of transportation hasn’t been developed yet.
: But-
: Anyway! I must be going now, but I’m sure you’ll be able to find the way here on your own! Bye, Jeeves!
: Tsu-
: ...kasa.
Sighing to myself and wondering whether or not the act of teleportation will ever again be touched on, I set off toward Tsukasa’s apartment.

And while I’m willing to chalk that last visit up to just one more strange, paranormal occurrence in a life that is now full of them, I’d more than welcome additional instances of that one in the future.
Because at least that one makes my life easier and doesn’t pressure me into violating every single girl I come across.
: Jeeves!
As I step into the room, I think about how this would look to everyone else.
Would they be surprised to see that I have fallen this far? Would they shrug it off and trick themselves into believing there’s nothing to it whatsoever?
Or would they be excited to be shown a glimpse into a life even darker than the ones I’ve stolen all the lights from?
I think the answer would differ from person to person.
Right now, though, the ones who I most want to see me are the ones who would take me away.
The Toukas and Futabas. The Norikos and Nikis. And everyone in between who pretends that a moral compass always points northbound when, sometimes, compasses just don’t work.
Right now, I am lost.
And all I can do is hope that this unlikely candidate can point me back in the right direction.
: This...looks different from the other rooms.
: Cool, right? I hired a team of designers to make it look as close to the living quarters of an “average commoner girl” as possible.
: And...their idea of “average commoner girl” included suits of armor, crystal chandeliers, and a suitcase full of money?
: The suitcase I brought from home. I intended to order a “pizza” today and am not sure what the going rate for those in today’s economy is.
: Well, I’m sorry to break it to you, but you might need another suitcase.
: Wow. Life must be really scary out here, huh?
: Yeah. But if worse comes to worst, we can always sell our crystal chandeliers.
: Exactly! And here you were insinuating that my designers were not accurately replicating the ideal commoner apartment!
: So, remember how I was talking about how your next lesson should be on sarcasm?
: That sounds so boring, though. I want to learn about math.
: Then there is a certain glasses-sporting porn shop employee I think you should meet as you two would get along very well.
: What’s a “porn shop?”
: Nothing. Anyway, time to learn things.
: You can not just pique the curiosity of a girl as adventurous and excitable as me and then pull the rug out, Jeeves. I could have your hands for such a thing.
: Or you could forget I said anything at all and we could start fresh right now. Hi. I’m Sensei. I’m here to teach you stuff.
: About porn?
: Do you have, like...a spray bottle I could shoot you with every time you say something you’re not supposed to say?
: Do I look like a cat to you?
: Unfortunately, yes. But there’s a certain level of nuance to that answer that even years worth of careful tutoring would not help you understand. Or would. But that makes it even worse.
: I’m starting to think we’re not going to be learning about math today either.
: And I’m starting to think this was a very bad idea.
: Like I said on the phone, I’m surprised you even called again. But that’s also what I said last time, so I guess you’re just full of surprises, aren’t you?
: Yeah, but not really in a good way.
: I’ll say. The last person who touched my head like that was eaten by an Irish bloodhound.
: Okay. Let’s move on.
: Good idea! I’ll get on the bed!
: That’s not what I-
: Come on, Jeeves! It’ll be just like last time! And this time, you have nowhere to run!
: That’s not a good thing...
: So, I’ve been thinking.
: That’s new.
: And that’s rude. But what I mean is I’ve been thinking about you.
: That’s worrying.
: And that’s confusing. But what I mean by that is that I don’t really think you’re cut out to be my tutor, Jeeves. So I’m going to have to let you go. I’m sorry it had to end this way.
: All things considered, this is probably the best way this could have ended. So thanks, I guess.
: You probably could have told me that before I came all the way over here, though.
: I could have. But it would have likely prevented you from hearing my new job offer.
: New job offer?
: Of associate executive literary entertainment coordinator.
: Pass.
: But I haven’t even described the job yet!
: Yeah, but the title is too long and I know you’d just make me say it all the time.
: It fits your interests a lot better, though! I’m doing this for you!
: What?
: Jeeves, as both your previous and future employer, it’s only right that I be honest with you. And the truth is that I never wanted to let you go at all.
: You just told me I wasn’t cut out for this like five seconds ago.
: Sometimes, being a CEO means making hard decisions. And also lying repeatedly until you’re caught and the business gets dragged under and you have to file for chapter 11.
: ...Okay?
: I still want you to be my teacher. But I don’t think you want to be my teacher. So I thought I’d give you a job that better aligns with your specific interests.
: ...What?
: Jeeves, I am a rather extraordinary individual. To be frank, I’m very impressive. But the only time you seemed impressed the other day was when I was talking about books.
: That’s just...what I’m good at, Tsukasa.
: Math and science are important too, yeah. And it does impress me that you’re willing to dive into physics and astronomy at your age, but...those things are different.
: Anyone can memorize formulas and...star maps or whatever, but not everyone can understand people. And doing that is the key to getting what you want out of life.
: Maybe. Probably. But also, you probably shouldn’t take my word for that as I still have no idea what I want out of life and I am much older than you.
: What direct correlation does literature have to people, though? I was under the impression that books were just tools used to get certain themes or ideas across.
: And to an extent, they are. But they’re also windows into the way an author views the world. Which, in turn, helps us compare and contrast our thoughts and values with theirs. Do you get it?
: I think so. But isn’t that still just like dissecting an animal at the end of the day? We’re still trying to figure something out by reading, aren’t we?
: Look at this way — what’s your favorite book?
: The Secret Garden by Frances Hodgson Burnett.
: That’s...depressing. And it makes my next question feel kind of loaded, but...how does reading that book make you feel?
: Free.
: Again, dark. But still, you felt something, didn’t you?
: Oh, so the feeling you get is the important part! Not the underlying message!
: They’re both important, but that’s what sets literature apart from science. There’s an element of humanity to it that other subjects lack.
: And I don’t know how possible it is to ever be happy if you can’t first grasp just how important one’s humanity is.

: There are a million complex equations out there, and it takes amazing people to solve the vast majority of them. But we are perhaps the most complex equation of all. And many just...lose sight of that.
: The only reason I even started tutoring was because I wanted to...test that, I guess.
: Because learning the way other people see things makes more sense to me than learning why Sirius is so bright. Or why water somehow keeps sandcastles standing.
: So you became a tutor because you wanted to understand people better?
: I...think so?
: I just...kind of said that without thinking much.
: That’s very interesting, Jeeves. I’ve never approached literature with that perspective before, but I’ll be sure to think more about my feelings moving forward.
: Do whatever you want. I’m just one person with one outlook when things come down to it. And the idea that anyone would be willing to listen to that at all still shocks me sometimes.
: I’m the same way, though.
: What do you mean?
: I mean I’m confused about why you’re even spending time with me in the first place.
: Nobody’s ever given me this much attention before, and I’m not even asking you to. You’re just doing it on your own.
: Well, either that or Mother put you up to it. But you’re the one who’s been calling me. Even if I previously commanded you to take the lead in terms of my education.
: And while it’s nice...and fun...to be spending time with you...
: It just makes me feel like you want something.
: I hope it’s just a different perspective. And if that’s the case, I’ll know why you chose me.
: But, based on personal experience, a person’s wants are never that simple. And, like you said the other day, leveraging a person’s weaknesses allows you to take advantage of them.
: I’ve got a lot of weaknesses when I really think about it, Jeeves.
: You could use me for anything you want and nobody would even care.
: Please don’t say things like that...
: But it’s the truth.
: I’m just a failsafe, remember? Disposable.
: You could lock me in a cage and none of my family would even know about it for months.
: In fact, it feels like that’s what they want sometimes. All I do is annoy them. And it’s probably the same for you.
: So if you want something, just say it. You’ve been nice enough to me lately that I wouldn’t mind giving it to you so long as it’s in my power to do so.
: You’ve more than earned it, Jeeves. I mean it.
: Even if it’s something irrational.
: Even if it’s something evil.
: Even if it’s something the world would scorn you for that you’ve wanted to take ever since you first laid eyes on it.
: No one cares about me.
: We can do it right here.
: You can lock me in a cage.
: Jeeves?...
: I just...
: I want to know if this is real or not.
: I’m sorry for asking this so bluntly, but...
: Do you...like me?
Pull the plug
: Let’s end here for today.
Tsukasa’s affection has increased to [tsukasa_love]!
Take it
: I’m doing this because I want to.
: No one else is making me.
Tsukasa’s affection has increased to [tsukasa_love]!
